newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Globus plans $10 mln capex as demand booms.
newsitem.headline: Globus plans $10 mln capex as demand booms.

text.p: Hungarian canned food firm Globus Rt plans acquisitions worth at least $10 million to meet increased demand for its products, the company's CEO said on Tuesday.
"We simply cannot produce as much as we could sell," Istvan Temesfoi told Reuters in an interview.
He said Globus's current capacity was some 60,000 tonnes per year while he estimated demand at between 120,000 and 150,000 tonnes.
This had led the company's management to consider the purchase other canning factories later this year, Temesfoi said, adding that targets could include both domestic and foreign companies.
"We already have a plant in the Ukraine and we are not only contemplating domestic purchases," he said.
Temesfoi added that virtually the entire Hungarian canning industry was up for sale and he had had offers from most of the plants.
Planned plant purchases will be funded via a capital increase, which would also include a public offering.

On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Globus shares have risen 180 percent this year to 2,540 forints on Tuesday from a low of 905 forints on January 6, even outperforming the BUX Index which rose some 80 percent over the same period.
Temesfoi added that while he was pleased to see the rise in the Globus share price this year, he was aware of the fact that the shares were illiquid.

"We could do (the capital increase) via a private placement only, but we have convinced prospective financial investors that making shares available on the markets would benefit the share," Temesfoi said.
Globus shares are also listed on the Frankfurt and Munich bourses.
Globus has managed to stay on a firm footing despite a shrinking domestic market, Temesfoi said, mainly by virtue of streamlining operations and upgrading the distribution network.
"The domestic market for canned food shrunk some 30 percent from 1995 to 1996 but Globus only lost five percent of its domestic sales (in volume terms)," he said.
Temesfoi, who recently acquired a 46 percent controlling stake in the company, said the increased demand would also show in Globus' 1997 earnings and sales, which will be considerably above plans.
"Sales will reach 7.2 to 7.5 billion forints this year," Temesfoi said, adding that the 1997 sales plan was 6.4 billion forints and in 1995 Globus had sales of 5.6 billion forints.
Profits were expected to rise to some 250 million forints this year compared with the earlier forecast of 195 million forints and last year's profit of 169 million forints.
Globus sells some 70 percent of its products in Hungary, while its main export markets are Germany and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
